I agree with what you're saying, but there is a double, confusing standard there. People always upvote stuff they like (e.g. a funny comment). So, it's natural that downvote then means dislike.

Some people think we should separate the two concepts: voting for worthwhileness and voting for rating. So, I could give a comment I don't like a low rating, but not vote on its worthwhileness. Or, if there was a comment I found amusing, I'd give it a good rating, but maybe mark it not worthwhile 'cause, in the grand scheme of things, it's probably not worth anyone's time. With comments, I wonder if the downvoat option shouldn't be done away with altogether. Someone says something of low value, spammish, circle jerky (thats a word, right?) or off topic...add your comment and tell them why their comment is such. Someone says something you don't agree with, add you comment telling them why you disagree. Let contribution frame the worthiness of the comment, not the downvoat option. It would force the lurkers who don't contribute but just downvoat to either stay lurking or get involved. It would require someone to put their money where their mouth is and use their words to disagree.

Of course I could see that devolving into long threads where all people do is argue back and forth, "Well, your comment is stupid" "Oh yeah, well you didn't say why my comment was stupid, so you're stupid" and repeat ad nauseum.

The main thing for me is to somehow ensure that dissenting opinions don't get downvoated into oblivion...not sure best way to stop that from happening.
